_comment: POST-HOC analyses, specified on 2026-10-13 after the frozen primary analysis (configs/protocol.json) had been completed and reported, in response to a pre-submission review. They add baselines and sensitivity analyses; they do not alter any primary result or any choice in protocol.json. Every post-hoc model uses the frozen splits, inner folds, selection objective, checkpoint/threshold rules, cross-fitting recipe and final seeds of protocol.json.
rationale: Labels are near step functions (median onset 82 s; 9/35 sessions never report discomfort) and 29 of 35 selected configurations of the primary analysis use the exposure feature sets; an exposure-time-only model is therefore the natural minimal baseline.

Time-LR.note: logistic regression on elapsed time only (class weight 5); full C grid

TimeGame-HGB.note: gradient boosting on elapsed time and game (game-specific, non-linear onset curves); same HGB space and budget as the primary analysis

multiplicity: Holm step-down adjustment over the six paired comparisons of E-DDQN with the other primary models, per operating rule (group-bootstrap p-values)
grouping_sensitivity: paired bootstrap resampling sessions (35 units) instead of linkage groups (21 units)
leave-one-group-out jackknife of each model's 5:1 cost and of the paired cost differences
always_alarm_comparison: paired group bootstrap of each model's D1 cost against the always-alarm policy

cost_curves.threshold: for each ratio R, the threshold minimising R*FN+FP on the pooled inner-OOF seed-ensemble scores of each outer fold's development groups (validation only), applied to that outer-test fold
cost_curves.normalisation: test cost divided by the cost of the better trivial policy at the same R (always alarm or never alarm)

review_round_2._comment: Specified on 2026-10-14 after a structured pre-submission review of the manuscript, when all other results were known. Computed only from the saved per-sample predictions and selected configurations; no model is trained or re-tuned and no primary result changes.
review_round_2.within_fold_roc_auc: ROC-AUC computed within each outer-test fold and averaged over folds (and over seeds for the seed-mean value), reported next to the pooled ROC-AUC, which combines the scores of five fold-specific models
review_round_2.group_sign_flip_test: exact two-sided sign-flip permutation test of the pooled D1 cost difference (seed ensembles) with the 21 linkage groups as units: statistic sum_g eps_g D_g / N over all 2^21 sign vectors; E-DDQN vs every other model (Holm over the six primary comparisons) and every model vs always alarming (Holm over the nine models); also the exposure-time baselines versus the random forest
review_round_2.feature_set_association: exploratory: within-fold ROC-AUC (seed mean) of each primary model and outer fold versus whether the selected feature set contains the 11 questionnaire (CSPQ) indicators; deviation from the fold mean over the seven primary models
review_round_2.search_space_sizes: number of distinct configurations in each family's search space (configs/protocol.json), to qualify 'same number of configurations'
review_round_2.search_draw: feature sets among each family's random-search candidates (results/hpo_results.csv) and, for E-DDQN, the lowest validation cost of candidates with and without the questionnaire indicators per outer fold

_later_additions._comment: Recorded on 2026-10-14 for transparency. The keys 'families', 'multiplicity', 'grouping_sensitivity', 'always_alarm_comparison' and 'cost_curves' were committed before the corresponding analyses were run. The analyses listed here were added afterwards without prior commitment; they are reported as post hoc in the paper (limitation iv; Supplementary Sec. S5).
while_writing_up: paired comparisons of the exposure-time baselines with the primary models (cost and ROC-AUC, group bootstrap)
label-dynamics summary (descriptive statistics of the data)
seed-ensemble block of the main results table (descriptive)

Holm adjustment over the nine models of the always-alarm comparison (the committed 'always_alarm_comparison' has no adjustment, and 'multiplicity' covers only the six comparisons with E-DDQN); added when the comparison was run
final_pre_submission_check: score scale of rule D0: where the untuned cut-off p_hat >= 1/6 lies on P(y=1|s) given each selected configuration's training class mix and loss (descriptive, no training; scripts/14_score_scale.py; Supplementary S5.12)

decision rule R3 of 'search_draw_sensitivity' implemented as |gap| <= 0.03, as specified ('within 0.03 of DQN's'); the first implementation tested gap <= 0.03 only. The outcome ('supported', gap 0.026) is unchanged.

search_draw_sensitivity._comment: Specified on 2026-10-14 after all other results were known, in response to the second-round pre-submission review, and committed BEFORE any of these runs. Question: does E-DDQN's result depend on its single random search draw, which offered only 2 exposure-only configurations (DQN: 6)? Every result is reported whatever it shows; no draw is selected; the primary results are not replaced.
search_draw_sensitivity.protocol: identical to configs/protocol.json: same splits, inner folds, training seed for the search (hpo_seed 777), budget (16 configurations), selection rule (pooled inner-OOF minimum 5:1 cost, ties PR-AUC), checkpoint rule, cross-fitting, final seeds 1000-1004 and threshold rules. Perturbation variants are not scored.

analysis: per variant: seed-mean D1 5:1 cost, seed-mean pooled ROC-AUC, within-fold ROC-AUC (seed mean), seed-ensemble D1 cost, selected feature set and discount factor per outer fold, and the number of exposure-only candidates in the draw

per pair: seed-ensemble D1 cost difference E-DDQN minus DQN with a 2,000-replicate group bootstrap (95% CI, two-sided p; seed 5) and an exact group sign-flip test; pooled ROC-AUC difference with a group bootstrap (seed 6)

decision_rules.R1_headline: The claim 'E-DDQN does not outperform the standard DQN' is challenged if, in any pair, E-DDQN's seed-ensemble D1 cost is lower than DQN's and the group-bootstrap 95% CI of the difference excludes zero.
decision_rules.R2_draw_dependence: E-DDQN's result is called draw-dependent if, across its three full-space draws, its seed-mean D1 cost spans more than 0.05 or its within-fold ROC-AUC spans more than 0.05.
decision_rules.R3_feature_set: Under the exposure-only restriction: if E-DDQN's within-fold ROC-AUC is within 0.03 of DQN's, the feature-set/search-draw explanation of Section V-G is supported; if it is more than 0.05 below DQN's, that explanation is insufficient and other components of E-DDQN remain plausible contributors; otherwise inconclusive.

threshold_scale_sensitivity._comment: Specified on 2026-10-21 after all other results were known, in response to an internal pre-submission review that noted the scale mismatch below; committed BEFORE the computation was run. Computed only from the saved per-inner-model validation and test scores of the final runs; no model is trained or re-tuned, no threshold is re-chosen, and no primary result is replaced. Every result is reported whatever it shows.
threshold_scale_sensitivity.question: The D1 threshold of each (family, outer fold, seed) is chosen on pooled OOF scores, each produced by ONE inner model, but applied to the outer-test score, which is the MEAN of the 3 inner models' scores. How much do the reported D1 results depend on this scale difference?
threshold_scale_sensitivity.variant_single_model: apply the unchanged D1 threshold of each (family, fold, seed) to each inner model's own test score separately (the scale on which the threshold was chosen); 5:1 cost, recall and false-positive rate pooled over the 5 outer folds per (seed, inner model), then averaged over the 3 inner models and the 5 seeds; compared with the reported seed-mean D1 results (pipeline recomputed from the same files as a check)
threshold_scale_sensitivity.spread_diagnostic: per (family, fold, seed): SD of the averaged test score divided by the mean SD of the single-model test scores (values below 1 = shrinkage by averaging); summarized by median and range per family
threshold_scale_sensitivity.reporting: descriptive, no test; the change in cost, recall and false-positive rate per family, and the spread ratio; stated in the limitation on threshold transfer and in the supplement (shortened version)

all_family_search_draws._comment: Specified on 2026-10-28 after all other results were known, in response to an internal pre-submission review (round 5) that noted that only E-DDQN and the standard DQN had been re-drawn, so that the E-DDQN vs random-forest result and the rankings of the other families might depend on their single draw. Committed BEFORE any of these runs and before any of the analyses under 'saved_prediction_analyses' were computed. Every result is reported whatever it shows; no draw is selected; the primary results are not replaced.
all_family_search_draws.protocol: identical to configs/protocol.json and to search_draw_sensitivity: same splits, inner folds, search training seed (777), per-family budget (16 configurations; 12 for LogReg), selection rule, checkpoint rule, cross-fitting, final seeds 1000-1004 and threshold rules; perturbation variants are not scored.

analysis: A. Per variant: seed-mean D1 5:1 cost (+-SD), seed-ensemble D1 cost, seed-mean pooled ROC-AUC, within-fold ROC-AUC (seed mean), selected feature sets.

B. Draw-matched comparisons: for each draw d = 1, 2, 3, E-DDQN draw d minus each of the six other families' draw d: seed-ensemble D1 cost difference with a 2,000-replicate group bootstrap (95% CI, two-sided p; seed 5) and the exact group sign-flip test; Holm adjustment over the six comparisons within each draw, separately for each test.

C. Draw-averaged comparisons (the main analysis of this experiment): for every family, the per-sample 5:1 cost averaged over the seed-ensemble D1 decisions of its three draws; E-DDQN minus each of the six other families, with the group bootstrap (seed 5) and the exact sign-flip test; Holm over the six comparisons, separately for each test.
D. Draw-averaged comparison of every family (seven) with always alarming, same tests, Holm over the seven comparisons.
E. Rank of the seven families by seed-ensemble D1 cost within each draw (descriptive).

decision_rules.A1_rf_robustness: The E-DDQN vs random-forest cost difference reported for the primary draw is called robust to the search draw only if the draw-averaged difference (C) is significant after Holm adjustment under BOTH the group bootstrap and the sign-flip test; otherwise it is called draw-specific.
decision_rules.A2_eddqn_better: The statement that E-DDQN does not outperform another family is challenged for a family X if the draw-averaged difference E-DDQN minus X is negative and significant after Holm adjustment under both tests.
decision_rules.A3_draw_dependence: A family is called draw-dependent if, across its three draws, its seed-mean D1 cost spans more than 0.05 or its within-fold ROC-AUC spans more than 0.05 (rule R2 of search_draw_sensitivity applied to every family).
decision_rules.A4_always_alarm: The statement that no model is shown to beat always alarming (linkage groups as units) stands unless a family's draw-averaged cost (D) is lower than always alarming and significant after Holm adjustment under both tests.

saved_prediction_analyses._comment: Computed from the saved primary predictions only; no model is trained. Specified in the same commit, before computation.
saved_prediction_analyses.B1_minimum_detectable_effect: For each of the six primary seed-ensemble comparisons with E-DDQN (draw 1) and each draw-averaged comparison (C): minimum detectable difference at 80% power and two-sided alpha 0.05, approximated as (1.960 + 0.842) x the SD of the 2,000 group-bootstrap replicates of the paired difference; for the 5:1 cost and for the pooled ROC-AUC difference (bootstrap seed 6).
saved_prediction_analyses.B2_seed_mean_paired_tests: E-DDQN minus each of the six other primary families, on the per-sample 5:1 cost averaged over the five seeds' own D1 decisions (seed-mean analogue of the primary test): group bootstrap (seed 5), exact sign-flip test, Holm over the six comparisons.
saved_prediction_analyses.B3_ensemble_vs_seed_mean: Descriptive, for each primary family: recall and false-positive rate under the seed-mean (per-seed D1) and seed-ensemble decisions; ratio of the SD of the ensemble test scores to the mean SD of the per-seed test scores; and the position of the ensemble D1 threshold relative to the range of the per-seed D1 thresholds.

decision_rules.F1_inputs_explain_deficit: E-DDQN's primary ranking deficit is called explained by its inputs if, with exposure features only, its within-fold ROC-AUC is within 0.03 of the median of the other six families' exposure-only within-fold ROC-AUC; not explained if it is more than 0.05 below; otherwise inconclusive.
decision_rules.F2_algorithm_difference: With inputs fixed, a cost difference between E-DDQN and another family is called established only if it is significant after Holm adjustment under both tests.

fixed_epoch.note: The configuration-selection optimism of Supplementary Sec. S9.5 (E-DDQN +0.288) also contains the selection of the configuration itself, which this check does not remove; it isolates checkpoint selection.

decision_rules.C1_checkpoint_explains_optimism: Checkpoint selection is called a substantial source of E-DDQN's optimism if its threshold optimism with the last epoch is less than half of that with the selected checkpoint; otherwise it is not.

event_level.question: How do the detectors behave when alarms are counted as events with a refractory period and onsets as the unit of detection?

definitions.alarm_event: an alarm event is raised at a second at which the D1 decision (seed ensemble) is 'alarm' and no alarm event was raised in the preceding R seconds of the same session
definitions.R: refractory period R = 60 s (primary); 30 s and 120 s (sensitivity)
definitions.onset: the first second with y = 1 in a session; sessions without any y = 1 have no onset
definitions.detected_onset: an alarm event occurs within [onset - 60 s, onset + 30 s]
definitions.lead_time: onset time minus the time of the first alarm event in that window (positive = before the reported onset)
definitions.false_alarm_event: an alarm event at a second with y = 0 that is not in [onset - 60 s, onset]; rate per 10 minutes of y = 0 time
definitions.event_cost: per session: 5 x missed onsets + false alarm events; mean over sessions

event_level.models: the seven primary families (seed ensembles, rule D1), Time-LR and always alarming
event_level.analysis: per model: onset detection rate, median lead time, false-alarm events per 10 min, mean event cost with a 95% group-bootstrap interval (seed 7); E-DDQN minus each other primary family: event-cost difference (group bootstrap, exact sign-flip, Holm over six).

decision_rules.E1_useful_operating_point: A model is called to reach a useful event-level operating point at R = 60 s if it detects at least 80% of onsets with at most one false alarm event per 10 minutes of non-event time.
